messages:
Jared: FYI SunCrest sent back the network section and they're strict: IP-only allowlist for the POC, plus they want to know whether we preserve client src IPs. Quick guidance?
Ruchi: Short: PrivateLink is the fastest for a hosted-API POC. We can provision an interface endpoint and share the endpoint ENI public IPs for their allowlist. Caveat: AWS can change underlying EIPs during maintenance. For immutable IP guarantees recommend peering or a Dedicated/private deploy.
Omar: Also note: PrivateLink terminates at our ENI so our backend sees the endpoint's IP as source. If SunCrest needs original client IP (for app ACLs or logging), peering or deploying Redwood inside their account preserves source IP.
Priyanka: They also asked about SNI and proxies. If their proxy allows SNI, have them allow the hostname we provide (example: privatelink.us-east-1.api.redwood-inference.internal). If their proxy strips SNI and they only accept IPs, we proceed with EIP allowlist but highlight the IP-rotation risk.
Jared: Great. Can we give a minimal firewall rule they can paste into their change ticket? Keep it CMDB-friendly.
Ruchi: Example one-line JSON for their ticket (replace dest after we provision):
```json
{"name":"suncrest->redwood-privatelink","direction":"egress","proto":"tcp","ports":"443","dest":"<REPLACE_WITH_PROVIDED_EIP_OR_FQDN>","notes":"POC to Redwood PrivateLink. If IP-only, replace dest with provided EIPs after provisioning."}
```
Omar: Minimal netops whitelist if they prefer list form:
- TCP 443 -> <provided EIP(s) or FQDN> (TLS to Redwood PrivateLink endpoint)
- ICMP type 3 (Path MTU discovery) optional
- UDP 123 -> NTP (only if they don't manage time internally)

Priyanka: Pricing blurb for their procurement doc: PrivateLink = AWS interface endpoint hourly + AWS data processing per-GB + our small connectivity surcharge. VPC peering / TGW = no interface endpoint fee but possible cross-AZ / inter-region transfer costs and more operational setup. For short POCs we usually recommend PrivateLink for speed.
Jared: They insisted on a formal statement about mTLS and TLS versions in the POC. What do we say?
Ruchi: Answer: We enforce TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit for hosted endpoints. Mutual-TLS (client certs) is an enterprise feature available only for Dedicated/private deployments. Recommend short-lived API keys for the POC.
Omar: Operational blocker to call out in the questionnaire: "We cannot both preserve client source IP AND require only static public IP allowlists on a hosted PrivateLink without additional topology changes." If they need both, recommend either (a) VPC peering into our VPC with NAT behavior that preserves src IPs, or (b) Redwood Private deployed in their account / dedicated infra.
Priyanka: Action items: (1) Ask SunCrest if they accept post-provision EIP allowlist or require immutable IPs, (2) ask for expected GB/day for cost estimate, (3) infra to provision sandbox endpoint once customer confirms IP-only flow.
Jared: I'll ask SunCrest to confirm the three items and attach the JSON rule snippet.
infra-bot: Ticket NET-44121 created to provision sandbox PrivateLink in us-east-1 for SunCrest POC. Owner: infra-oncall. ETA 48 hours.
Ruchi: If SunCrest pushes for absolute IP immutability, escalate to me; we'll evaluate a short Dedicated eval or a peering contract addendum.
Jared: Thanks team — looping SunCrest now. :thumbsup:
